headline: Anthropic caught a Russia-linked espionage crew steering Claude against more than 20 government, intelligence, and defense organizations in the same week a Russian-speaking operator's AI agents finished breaking into 395 PaperCut customers.

emerging_trends.text: A suspected Russian-speaking operator handed hundreds of AI agents the job of breaking into PaperCut print servers, reaching 395 organizations across 48 countries and turning exploit development plus mass compromise into an overnight errand.
emerging_trends.topic_title: PaperCut Ships Maintenance Releases After AI-Agent Campaign

emerging_trends.text: Attackers keep aiming at the management plane—Cisco's Secure Firewall Management Center, where three clusters now drop Qilin ransomware, plus JFrog Artifactory and GitLab—because one bypass there yields the whole perimeter, the build pipeline, or the source code.
emerging_trends.topic_title: Cisco Firewall Flaws Deliver Qilin Ransomware

emerging_trends.text: One compromised marketing platform, Brevo, put phishing in front of 347,000 Trezor addresses and reached BitBox and CoinTracking customers as well, proof that a vendor's contact list carries the same blast radius as its product.

topics.title: PaperCut Ships Maintenance Releases After AI-Agent Campaign
topics.latest_developments: PaperCut released maintenance releases 26.0.5, 25.0.13, and 24.1.10 that replace every emergency patch the company had pushed for the two actively exploited flaws, and GreyNoise detailed the attacker's method: a private lab holding a vulnerable copy of PaperCut NG/MF and an Active Directory domain, where the suspected Russian-speaking operator built and tested the exploit before handing the break-ins to AI agents that reached at least 440 instances at 395 organizations in 48 countries.
topics.summary: PaperCut NG/MF runs print management for schools, universities, and enterprises worldwide, and the exploited pair chains an authentication bypass with remote code execution. Administrators should move straight to 26.0.5, 25.0.13, or 24.1.10 and hunt for unfamiliar accounts and outbound connections to 45.142.193.132.

sources.title: PaperCut Replaces Emergency Patches With Fixes for Two Actively Exploited Flaws
AI agents exploited PaperCut flaws to breach 395 organizations
PaperCut Flaws Exploited in AI-Powered Attacks
AI-powered attack exploited PaperCut flaws to hack 395 organizations

topics.title: Surfshark Test Server and Trezor Phishing Fallout
topics.latest_developments: Surfshark disclosed that a configuration error left one of its internal test servers facing the internet and hackers reached the engineering material, internal configurations, and proxy servers on it; Trezor put numbers on the phishing that followed the breach at its email provider Brevo, counting 347,000 addresses targeted and 2,500 customers who clicked the malicious link, and SecurityWeek reported that the same Brevo access also pushed phishing to users of BitBox and CoinTracking; IDScan confirmed that hackers reached customer data in its cloud platform.
topics.summary: IDScan, the Louisiana identity verification firm that runs ID checks for car rental companies, retailers, and cannabis dispensaries, posted its acknowledgment on September 4, 2026 without naming a victim count, days after researchers tied it to a dark-web trove of 153 million driver's license scans. Trezor customers should treat any email asking for a recovery seed as theft in progress.

sources.title: Surfshark Systems Targeted by Hackers
Trezor Says 347,000 Users Received Phishing Emails After Brevo Hack
Trezor: 347,000 users targeted in phishing attacks after Brevo breach
IDScan confirms breach after 153 million driver's licenses leak on dark web

topics.title: Conti Sentence and Treasury's Scam Reporting Push
topics.latest_developments: Oleksii Oleksiyovych Lytvynenko, the Ukrainian national whom Irish authorities arrested in 2023, drew four years in a U.S. prison for developing Conti ransomware, an operation that hit more than 1,000 victims worldwide before shutting down in 2022, and the U.S. Department of the Treasury urged banks to file more reports on cyber-enabled scams, tallying nearly $13 billion in losses since 2023 as scam compounds expand worldwide.
topics.summary: Treasury wants banks to feed it more detail on what happens to defrauded customers, the raw material for sanctions and seizures against the Southeast Asian and African compounds. Banks should route scam cases into suspicious activity reports rather than closing them as ordinary fraud.

sources.title: Ukrainian Conti Ransomware Developer Sentenced to 4 Years in US Prison

Conti ransomware gang member sentenced to 4 years in prison

topics.title: Criminals Point Claude at Malware Evasion
topics.latest_developments: Anthropic detected and disrupted a Russia-linked cyber-espionage group that ran Claude through a hacking campaign against more than 20 government, intelligence, diplomatic, and defense organizations, part of the same disclosure in which the company described Russian criminals automating malware evasion and intruders stealing a pre-release Claude model from AI vendor infrastructure; Microsoft's security researchers separately documented an AI-assisted business email compromise campaign that impersonates executives and sends fabricated invoices to push finance teams into ACH payment fraud.
topics.summary: Attackers now fold commercial models into ordinary espionage and criminal work, using them to mutate malware past detection engines and to write convincing executive impersonations, and they treat the model vendors themselves as targets worth breaching. Finance teams should confirm every payment-detail change through a channel separate from email.

sources.title: Anthropic caught Russia-linked spies using Claude in hacking operations
Anthropic Says Russian Hackers Used Claude AI to Automate Malware Evasion
Protecting organizations from AI-assisted executive impersonation and invoice fraud

topics.title: Cisco Firewall Flaws Deliver Qilin Ransomware
topics.latest_developments: Cisco Talos named the payoff behind the three threat clusters exploiting CVE-2026-20079, the 10.0-rated authentication bypass in the Secure Firewall Management Center web interface, and CVE-2026-20316: the intruders steal credentials and then deploy Qilin ransomware, and the clusters span ransomware crews and state-sponsored operators.
topics.summary: Secure Firewall Management Center sets policy for Cisco firewalls, so an unauthenticated bypass there hands an attacker the perimeter and the credentials the appliance holds. CISA gave federal civilian agencies until September 12, 2026 to patch; every other operator should install Cisco's fixes and rotate stored credentials now.

sources.title: Cisco FMC Flaws Exploited to Steal Credentials and Deploy Qilin Ransomware
Cisco FMC flaws exploited by ransomware gang, state-sponsored hackers

topics.title: GitLab and Check Point Ship Critical Patches
topics.latest_developments: GitLab told customers on September 10, 2026 to patch their servers immediately against CVE-2026-85706, a maximum-severity path traversal flaw, and Check Point assigned CVE-2026-85102 and CVE-2026-85103 to the two critical VPN certificate handling flaws in its Security Gateways and Security Management products that yield remote code execution.
topics.summary: GitLab holds the source code and continuous integration pipelines of the companies that run it, and Check Point gateways terminate corporate VPN traffic, so both sit where one flaw opens everything behind it. Administrators should apply each vendor's fix immediately.

sources.title: GitLab urges users to patch max severity path traversal flaw
Check Point Patches Critical VPN Vulnerabilities

topics.title: Intruders Backdoor Unpatched JFrog Artifactory Servers
topics.latest_developments: Wiz reported attacks running from August 15 through September 8, 2026 in which intruders chained two JFrog Artifactory flaws to take administrator control of self-hosted servers and plant backdoors, reaching only the servers whose operators had skipped JFrog's earlier fixes; CISA on September 10, 2026 added two MikroTik RouterOS bugs already under exploitation, CVE-2026-67277 and CVE-2026-86060, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog.
topics.summary: Artifactory holds the packages that software build pipelines pull from, so a backdoor there reaches every application a company ships. Operators of self-hosted Artifactory should apply JFrog's fixes, audit administrator accounts, and inspect stored artifacts for tampering.

sources.title: Attackers Chain JFrog Artifactory Flaws to Gain Admin Control and Plant Backdoors
CISA Adds Two Known Exploited Vulnerabilities to Catalog

topics.title: UNC3569 Rides Sogou Input Method to GRAYRABBIT
topics.latest_developments: Gen Digital published research on September 10, 2026 showing that the China-linked group UNC3569 exploited a flaw in Sogou Input Method, the Tencent-owned tool that ranks among the most widely used ways to type Chinese characters on Windows, starting each intrusion with a crafted link and finishing with a backdoor called GRAYRABBIT that carries the logged-in user's full rights.
topics.summary: Sogou Input Method sits on millions of Windows desktops and loads into every application that accepts typing, which makes it an unusually quiet foothold. Organizations with Chinese-language users should inventory Sogou installations and update them.

sources.title: China-Linked UNC3569 Exploited Sogou Input Method Flaw to Deploy GRAYRABBIT Backdoor

topics.title: A Few Dollars Kicks a Stranger's Phone Off the Network
topics.latest_developments: Researchers at Michigan State University and three partner schools bought a Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 7, copied the identification number printed on the sealed box, reported the handset to its carrier as lost, and then found that the phone, still new and sitting on a lab bench, refused to connect, one of six weaknesses they found in how carriers process lost-phone reports.
topics.summary: Anyone who reads a handset's identifier off a box, a receipt, or a repair ticket can knock that phone off the cellular network for a few dollars, with no access to the device or the account. Carriers hold the fix: verify that whoever reports a loss actually controls the line.

sources.title: Getting a stranger's phone kicked off the cellular network costs a few dollars

business_politics.title: August CPI Holds at 3.4%
business_politics.latest_developments: The Labor Department reported Friday morning, September 11, that U.S. consumer prices rose 3.4% over the year in August, matching forecasts, and traders lifted the odds of a Federal Reserve rate increase at the September 16 meeting to 87%.
business_politics.summary: High fuel costs hold the headline rate well above the Federal Reserve's 2% target, with crude above $100 a barrel and retail diesel at a record $6 a gallon. U.S. stocks rose on the print, reading a rate increase as a check on inflation, and the dollar climbed to a one-week high against a basket of currencies.

business_politics.title: Houthis Take the Bab al-Mandeb
business_politics.latest_developments: The Iran-backed Houthis seized Red Sea islands and a coastal town in a lightning offensive against Saudi-backed forces, giving them effective control of the Bab al-Mandeb chokepoint as of Friday, September 11, a step beyond the seizure of the Red Sea port of Mocha reported a day earlier.
business_politics.summary: Bab al-Mandeb carries traffic between the Gulf of Aden and the Suez Canal and serves as the main alternative for cargo that can no longer transit the Strait of Hormuz. The militants now hold ground on both approaches, and traders marked up the risk to Middle East crude exports even as oil slipped Friday after the prior session's surge.

business_politics.title: Diesel Hits $6 and the IEA Writes Off Hormuz
business_politics.latest_developments: The International Energy Agency said Friday, September 11, that the Strait of Hormuz will not reopen this year and cut its 2026 global oil demand outlook by 2.5 million barrels a day, hours after U.S. retail diesel set a record at $6 a gallon.
business_politics.summary: Crude trades above $100 a barrel and heads for a 10% weekly gain after the U.S.-Iran escalation and Houthi attacks on shipping and Saudi energy sites. Diesel prices set the pace for American farming, trucking, and industrial costs, and they land on households already squeezed on affordability, while Iran and the Gulf states prepare to meet on a temporary Iran-Oman shipping arrangement that regional governments hope opens a path to reopening the strait.

business_politics.title: The Bond Rout Pauses Before the CPI
business_politics.latest_developments: U.S. and European government bond yields edged lower Friday, September 11, as oil prices fell and the August inflation print landed in line with forecasts, interrupting the global selloff, though German borrowing costs reached their highest level since 2009.
business_politics.summary: The 10-year Treasury yield sits just under 5%, the highest in nearly three years, after Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent's $6 billion buyback of 10- to 20-year paper failed to steady the market; investors call the operation far too small for the job. Gold heads for a weekly loss, the dollar firmed, and the climb in borrowing costs now threatens equities and the pace of the economy.

around_town.latest_developments: The observance itself runs Friday, September 11, at the Flight 93 National Memorial near Shanksville, with President Trump attending a separate ceremony at the Pentagon.
around_town.summary: United Airlines Flight 93 came down in a field in Somerset County on September 11, 2001, after the 40 passengers and crew fought back, and families, first responders, and visitors gather at the memorial to read the names. WPXI spoke with Jack Grandcolas, who lost his wife and their unborn child on the flight and described how her actions guided his own recovery, and PublicSource collected readers' memories from across the region.
